(AI Generated).

## Freed v26.10.702-dev

Independent test credentials

### Features

- The isolated transfer-acceptance app can adopt a former Primary as a persistent read-only viewer, with native enforcement that also refuses automatic read and seen edits
- Linux stores Library signing keys in an existing unlocked Secret Service vault and preserves the same identity across app and vault restarts

### Fixes

- The transfer-acceptance app uses a new application identity and its own Library credential vault, preserving existing ordinary and preview installations
- Locked or unavailable Linux vaults return an error instead of replacing Library keys
- Transfer acceptance previews retain normal onboarding and Library selection without automatically creating a sample Library
- Desktop Settings shows the ten newest individual releases with complete notes
- Descriptions in sidebar tiles without media are centered
- Archiving from the reader, header, keyboard or feed hides the pending row immediately. A failed write restores the row and keeps the reader open
- Automatic development sample data can be disabled
- Compatible native dependencies include security updates
- The mobile PWA keeps the feed and inline reader on the document scroller when returning from a post

### Follow-ups

- Primary transfer remains disabled in ordinary builds. Synthetic handoff acceptance uses the separate signed transfer-acceptance app and a PWA built from the same release commit
- Installed acceptance across two independent Desktop installations and a matching PWA remains required before enabling ordinary transfer and recovery or moving an existing personal Library
- Verify the new acceptance identity on both Macs before enrolling a disposable Library. Packaging isolation does not establish installed transfer acceptance

### Downloads

**macOS:** `.dmg` (Apple Silicon or Intel, signed + notarized)  
**Windows:** `.exe` (NSIS installer)  
**Linux:** `.AppImage`  

> macOS downloads are signed and notarized for normal Gatekeeper installation.
